ftw_001: You can recognise it by its unusual height for a jujube, nearly 14 metres, with no fence or plaque marking it. It stands near the corner of Old Garden Road and Rock Springs Road, in the Botanic Garden.
ftw_002: You can recognise it by its very thick trunk, over six metres round, standing unfenced on a grass strip beside the road. It stands on Ward Parkway, between TCU and the Colonial Country Club.
ftw_003: You can recognise it by its very thick, gnarled trunk for a mesquite, nearly five metres round, standing free and unfenced. It stands on Will Rogers Road South, at the Will Rogers Memorial Center.
ftw_004: You can recognise it as the ash growing among the earliest graves. It stands in Pioneers Rest Cemetery, on Samuels Avenue.
